resale_co.name: Housing Certificate of Occupancy (HCO)
resale_co.valid_for: The certificate may be issued (or reissued at no charge) any time within 90 days after the inspection that confirms full compliance.
requirements: A new certificate is needed at every change of occupancy; no one may move in or place personal items in the home until inspections are passed
Application must list all occupants (name, age, gender) before the certificate is issued
Home must meet the Township housing chapter, local plumbing, building, electrical, fire, zoning, health and safety ordinances, and the New Jersey state housing standards
Housing Officer checklist (2016): septic certification and water test
Checklist: GFCI outlets in kitchen, bathrooms, laundry, garage and outside
Checklist: handrail to the basement and on porch and deck steps; emergency heater switch at the top of the stairs
Checklist: electrical box labeled, 100 amps or more; water heater relief piped down
Checklist: smoke detector at the top of the basement stairs and in a heated garage
Checklist: chimney certification (visual inspection by a heating contractor or chimney sweep); heater serviced and inspected
Checklist: roof, siding, windows, doors and screens in repair; house numbered; trash, debris and abandoned vehicles removed
Checklist: fire-resistant door and walls between an attached garage and the house

fees.label: Housing certificate of occupancy, single-family building (initial inspection and one follow-up)
fees.quote: (a) Single-family residential building consisting of one dwelling unit: $50

fees.label: Housing certificate of occupancy, each unit in a multi-unit building (initial inspection and one follow-up)
fees.quote: (b) Each residential dwelling unit in a multi-unit building: $50

fees.label: Each inspection visit after the first follow-up, paid in advance
fees.quote: The above fees are for the initial inspection visit and one follow-up inspection visit for each HCO application. An additional charge of $ 50 shall be charged and paid in advance for each subsequent inspection visit.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Certificate of Occupancy Application (check 'Sale Property', list the owner, all occupants and the agent) and give it with the $50.00 fee to Neal Sheppard, Housing/Zoning Officer, at 491 Route 45, Mannington, NJ 08079 (in person Wednesdays 9:00 to 11:00 AM, by mail, or at the Clerk's office or drop box). Questions: zoning@manningtontwp.com or 856-935-2359 x104 (leave a voicemail).

evidence.quote: A new HCO (or RCO, if applicable) shall be obtained each time there is a change of occupancy of any building, structure, dwelling, dwelling unit, hotel/motel, rooming house, rooming unit or any other unit or structure for residential purposes.
evidence.doc_date: 2018 (Ordinance No. 18-04; copy posted is the introduction version)

evidence.quote: An HCO may be issued (or reissued without additional charge) at any time within 90 days following the inspection visit at which full compliance is confirmed.
Note: Inspections must be completed and passed prior to occupancy or the placement of personal items within the dwelling.
Neal Sheppard - Housing/Zoning Officer ... 856-935-2359 x104 ♦ Fax: 856-935-6557 Hours: Wednesday 9:00 - 11:00 AM

resale_co.notes: Ordinance 18-04 amended Township code chapter 64 'Housing Standards' so that a housing certificate of occupancy is needed for every change of occupancy, not only rentals. The copy on the Township site is the introduction version with blank meeting dates; ecode360 search results (MA1835, not opened) show the same rules in the current code. The Housing Officer's email is hidden on the Township page by an email-protection script; it decodes to zoning@manningtontwp.com. The 2016 Housing Officer Checklist is a scanned PDF with no text layer; Claude read it page by page (2026-09-30). No lead time is stated. Construction permits are handled by the State of New Jersey (main office 609-567-3653; local office 856-935-2359 ext. 202, Wednesday mornings).

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many business days before closing you apply (more than 10, 4 to 10, under 4).

fees.label: State smoke/carbon monoxide certificate, applied more than 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: If you are applying for a certificate more than ten business days from the closing date the fee is $45 dollars

fees.label: State smoke/carbon monoxide certificate, applied 4 to 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: if applying 4 to 10 business days from the closing date the fee is $90

fees.label: State smoke/carbon monoxide certificate, closing less than 4 business days away
fees.quote: if the closing date is less than four business days the fee is $161.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'). Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email address is required. The certificate is emailed once the application is submitted, the fee is paid and any required inspections are done. Homes heated by electricity that do not need a carbon monoxide alarm should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.

fire_cert.notes: The State (NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety) is Mannington's fire code enforcing agency (registry code S; state directory code 1705) and is marked 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates) on the DCA's July 2026 state towns list; the DCA portal lists MANNINGTON TWP-001 under the State and not smoke-certificate exempt. The DCA online form is the Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance (CSACMASPSIL); it no longer includes a fire extinguisher, in line with P.L.2025, c.19. The state directory lists Louis Kilmer at (609) 633-6132; the DCA Bureau page lists him as Bureau Chief at (609) 633-6106, and the July 2026 state towns list calls him Deputy Division Director. Mannington Fire Co #1 (Chief Timothy Butcher) is the volunteer fire company, not an inspecting agency.
